claims.claim: Rachel made landfall in far northern Baja California on the evening of Oct 10 as a weakened tropical storm
Mexico's SMN says Rachel entered Mexican territory in the early hours of Oct 11 about 40 km south-southeast of Ensenada with 95 km/h sustained winds and 110 km/h gusts
At 21:00 Mexico City time Oct 11, post-tropical Rachel was 65 km southwest of Cabo San Quintín moving north-northeast at 57 km/h
claims.attributed_to: SMN/Conagua via La Hoja de Ruta

claims.claim: The NHC's final advisory at 8 a.m. MST Oct 11 said Rachel had dissipated over the southwestern U.S. with estimated intensity 30 kt
NHC advisory 56A put a tropical storm warning on the west coast of Baja California from Punta Eugenia to the U.S./Mexico border and on the east coast from Isla San Luis to Puerto Peñasco
Baja California's state government forecast winds of 60-80 km/h with gusts 80-140 km/h from Saturday night through Sunday and opened temporary shelters via DIF Baja California
SMN forecast 25-50 mm of rain in Baja California, gusts to 100 km/h and waves up to 6 m, warning of landslides and flooding in low-lying areas
Rachel prompted the second-ever tropical storm watch for California, covering San Diego County
NHC reported major coastal flooding already occurring with water levels up to 1.5 feet above predictions, expected to worsen at high tide
Rachel produced two deaths in Mexico from heavy rain and flash flooding, per the storm's Wikipedia article
No official Mexican government fatality or damage figure for Rachel was located; the 5 dead/5 missing tally is Wikipedia's
The Oct 11 SMN advisory was dominated by Hurricane Simon, Category 4, 95 km west of Manzanillo with 240 km/h sustained winds and 295 km/h gusts
Mexico's death toll from Tropical Storm Rachel rose to eight, all in Ensenada municipality, four of them minors, per General Daniel Gallegos Acevedo, commander of the Second Military Zone
claims.attributed_to: Gen. Daniel Gallegos Acevedo, SEDENA, via El País/EFE/Europa Press

claims.claim: Four deaths had been reported as of Monday; the toll was raised at a Wednesday press conference
The eighth victim was a 17-year-old boy whose body was found in Lomas de Mendoza
The other seven dead include three minors (ages 4, 13, 14), three women (two 30, one 35) and one 51-year-old man
Five of the eight dead belong to one family, the Burgos family of Hermosillo, Sonora
Two people remain unlocated per Gen. Gallegos; El País reports four still missing -- discrepancy unresolved
claims.attributed_to: Gen. Gallegos via info7; El País

claims.claim: A 10-year-old boy was found alive; 32 civilians were airlifted from Rancho Génesis (22 foreigners, 10 Mexicans)
Six shelters are active (four San Quintín, two Ensenada) and more than 3,500 troops and personnel are mobilized
Gov. Marina del Pilar Ávila says the emergency remains active and warned Simon could reach Baja California coasts Sunday
claims.attributed_to: Marina del Pilar Ávila via EFE/info7

claims.claim: Simon is Category 1, semi-stationary off Jalisco, not currently expected to make landfall; it caused one death in Chilpancingo and one in Mazatlán and closed at least seven ports
Tropical Storm Trudy formed Tuesday off southwestern Mexico and could intensify to a major hurricane by Friday
At least 370 homes damaged in Ensenada and 258 in San Quintín; agricultural losses preliminarily estimated at ~US$50 million
No Mexican federal government death-toll statement located; the eight-death figure comes from SEDENA's Second Military Zone commander and state officials
Mexico's death toll from Rachel rose to nine, four of them minors, all in Ensenada municipality, per the Baja California government and federal authorities
claims.attributed_to: Baja California government and federal authorities

claims.claim: Eight deaths had been announced at a Wednesday press conference by Gen. Daniel Gallegos Acevedo, commander of the Second Military Zone
The ninth victim was Rosa María Olivera Almazán, 44, found Wednesday near the Magaña bridge on the La Bufadora road in Maneadero
Search continues for Rosalinda Almazán, 24, reported missing
Two people remain unlocated per Gen. Gallegos; El País reports four still missing -- discrepancy unresolved
claims.attributed_to: Gen. Gallegos via info7; El País

claims.claim: Five of the dead are the Burgos Terán family of Hermosillo, Sonora, swept away in the El Pípila arroyo at Maneadero
claims.attributed_to: Europa Press citing Zócalo; Grupo Animal

claims.claim: Ensenada mayor Claudia Agatón Muñiz requested a disaster declaration

claims.attributed_to: State Bienestar secretariat via Europa Press and La Jornada

claims.attributed_to: Marina del Pilar Ávila via EFE/info7

claims.claim: The ninth victim was Rosa María Olivera Almazán, found Wednesday in Maneadero
Olivera Almazán was reported missing after being swept away Saturday night in Lomas de Mendoza
Eight deaths had been announced at Wednesday's press conference by Gen. Daniel Gallegos Acevedo

claims.attributed_to: Europa Press; Daily Star; El Universal; La Noticia Regional; La Jornada

claims.claim: Search continues for two unlocated per Gallegos; El País reports four still missing

claims.claim: Other identified dead include the Burgos Terán family of Maneadero, Valentín Lozano Gómez and Keila Azalea Sandria González; ages and name spellings vary across outlets
